title: Delegated data lifecycle templates and forensic hash-chaining for retention evidence
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Provide a reusable, delegated template system for per-route retention settings (prompts, responses, request logs, metrics) plus cryptographic evidence packaging using hash-chaining so that auditors can verify deletion/retention actions and chain-of-custody for exported bundles. Scope includes: template UI in Console, API for template assignment, scheduler for per-route deletion and TTL enforcement, evidence bundling with SHA-256 hash chain and signed attestations, and an evidence retrieval API for compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Admins can create and version delegation templates that specify retention windows and retention granularity for prompts, responses, request logs, and metrics
Templates can be applied to routes, tenants, or resource groups via Console UI and API; application shows effective retention per route
Automated per-route deletion scheduler runs and deletes data within configured SLO; successful deletions are recorded to evidence bundles
Evidence bundles include a manifest, per-file SHA-256 hashes, a chained hash summary (forensic chain), and a tamper-evident attestation signed with Redwood KMS
Evidence retrieval API returns a verifiable bundle and a short-lived download token; audit trail shows who requested and who applied the template
Design and implementation pass security review and threat modeling for HSM/KMS integration and export controls
Compatibility path for Dedicated and Private deployments documented (KMS integration points, network egress constraints)
technical_notes: Retention enforcement: combine time-indexed partitions for logs/metrics and manifest-driven deletion for object stores containing prompts/responses
Scheduler: orchestrated by retention-controller (ENG-4892) with per-tenant rate limiting and exponential backoff for transient failures

Evidence packaging: stage files into a temporary bucket, compute per-file SHA-256, produce a manifest JSON (minimal fields: path, file_size, sha256, deleted_by, deleted_at), compute chain-of-hashes by concatenating manifest entries in canonical order and hashing the concatenation
Attestation: sign the chain root with a dedicated KMS key; store attestation metadata in audit-log DB with retention aligned to policy
Proof verification: verification scripts will be published and open-sourced under redwood/retention-proof; include sample verifier for auditors
Privacy: PII redaction must run before any evidence export unless explicit customer opt-in is present; default export will mask sensitive tokens
On-prem/Dedicated: allow customers to supply KMS signing key URL (external KMS) and disable outbound evidence upload; support air-gapped evidence export via signed USB packaging instructions
design_decisions: Use template inheritance where route-level templates override tenant defaults to minimize admin burden
Evidence manifests are JSON-LD to remain human-readable and machine-verifiable
Choose SHA-256 for hashing due to interoperability and performance; switch to SHA-3 only if regulatory requires
Retention scheduler will prefer eventual consistency for bulk deletes to reduce read/write amplification on hot partitions
Expose minimal fields in Console to avoid accidental PII exposure; provide an advanced mode for compliance teams
tradeoffs: Immediate delete vs deferred delete: deferred deletions (soft-delete then purge) increase storage for a short window but significantly reduce chance of accidental permanent loss during retries
Strongly consistent attestations require synchronous KMS signing which adds latency; we accept asynchronous attestation with retry and status reconciliation to preserve throughput
Packaging runtime vs streaming proof: packaging into temporary buckets simplifies verification but increases temporary storage and network usage; streaming proofs are harder to verify by auditors
